solution:
Neither C nor E is an endpoint, and each has only two roads. Thus passing through C forces the segment B–C–D or its reverse; similarly E forces A–E–D or its reverse. Compressing these segments leaves two distinguishable A–D links, two distinguishable B–D links, and one A–B link.

First ignore the distinction between parallel links. If the route starts A–B, it must then go to D, visit A and return to D before ending at B (returning immediately to B would strand the A–D links). This gives A–B–D–A–D–B.

If it starts A–D–A, only A–B remains at A, giving A–D–A–B–D–B. If it starts A–D–B, the next move is to A or D, after which the rest is forced: A–D–B–A–D–B or A–D–B–D–A–B. These exhaust the four compressed sequences.

For each sequence, the direct A–D link can be used on either of the two A–D traversals, and independently the direct B–D link on either B–D traversal. Hence there are 4·2·2 = 16 routes.
Final answer: 16
